market_story: COAL — MISO's coal fleet is the oldest large block on the system (true cap-weighted vintage 1982, 33 GW past the age-40 escalation onset): a 43-year-old steamer carries a measurably higher forced-outage rate and a deeper performance derate than its nameplate suggests, so the real market has ~1.3 GW less coal capability in an average hour than a uniformly-young fleet would — the mid-merit coal the model was dispatching in those hours is, in reality, in the shop. ST_GAS — the 1976-vintage gas steamers are the fleet's most fragile class (age ~48, every MW past both onsets); their real availability is lower everywhere, which is part of why the real overnight/shoulder stack is thinner than the model's was. CT_PEAKER — the summer price-setter: the real CT fleet averages 26 years old with 85% of its capacity past the escalation onset, so on a July afternoon the real market has ~0.5 GW less peaking capability than a 15-year-old fleet would offer — the real supply curve runs out of cheap capability sooner, and the marginal unit sits higher up the stack, which is exactly the direction of MISO's observed summer prices. CC_REGULAR — mostly 2000s-vintage and barely past onset; the repair moves it least (+0.1 GW), consistent with CCs being the fleet's healthiest class in reality.
